tests.name: Effective description
tests.message: Verdict not allowed for this test: 'warning' (allowed: passed, failed)

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific throughout — it does not explain general concepts like what Bedrock or S3 are, and jumps straight into project-specific check-ids, routing rules, and AWS API behaviors that the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: Every assessment is grounded in the check catalog [checks-evaluation.md]... Each check carries a stable check-id, a severity, a detection rule, a remediation, and an AWS-doc citation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: While the body is long, it mostly avoids embedding large reference tables (check catalogs, metric thresholds, error tables) inline — those are consistently delegated to references/ files. The severity table and scope model are compact summaries, not detailed reference dumps.
tests.evidence: Walk [checks-evaluation.md](references/checks-evaluation.md) for the path you are on, applying each detection rule.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All seven files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Nearly every reference link is accompanied by an explicit condition for when to load it.
tests.evidence: "load it before assigning any check-id or severity" and "load before any log query or metric read" and "load when a truncation or finish-reason shift is in question"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only guardrails, finding format, delegation payload) are rigidly prescriptive, while flexible areas (synthesis, routing a question to a path) allow judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: "Read-only. Never call a mutating API" is exact and strict, while "A question can take more than one path; say which" allows flexibility in Step 1.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple paths exist (Bedrock vs SageMaker evaluation), the skill designates clear defaults per scenario and routes explicitly rather than presenting equal menus; service selection is rule-based, not a menu of options.
tests.evidence: "Service check. When a job is named, confirm which service ran it: sagemaker:DescribeTrainingJob for a recipe-driven job, bedrock:GetEvaluationJob for a Bedrock-native one"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (Steps 1-5) applicable to any evaluation incident or review, with specific details (templates, check-ids) embedded within that reusable structure.
tests.evidence: "Work the steps in order... Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support"

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive, concrete gotchas section covering non-obvious domain pitfalls specific to AWS evaluation APIs.
tests.evidence: "'ListEvaluationJobs' is empty, so no evaluation has ever run — CRITICAL.' Bedrock evaluation is region-gated... confirm regional support first and report INFO/advisory"

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured findings/reports and provides templates in assets/ for this purpose, referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: "load [evaluation-report-template.md](assets/evaluation-report-template.md) for the Bedrock path and the posture review"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The only inline template (the Findings block) is short (under 20 lines), with longer report templates properly moved to assets/.
tests.evidence:
```
Findings
<check-id> (<SEVERITY>) — <measured <value> | no-datapoints | not-queried> — <window> — <source API> — owner:<area> — <doc URL>
```

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three files in assets/ are referenced in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies the condition under which it should be loaded.
tests.evidence: "load when delegating evidence-gathering" and "load when the report covers the SageMaker path" and "load when a full written report is wanted"

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths rooted at assets/.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and the detailed sections below explicitly reference the same step numbers (Step 1, Step 2, etc.).
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support" followed by "### Step 1 — Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output for errors before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output" with checks like "Scan the draft for an upgraded negative, sentence by sentence" and "No unqualified negative survives in the prose."
